In [[algebraic geometry]] and [[synthetic differential geometry]], a '''Grothendieck connection''' is a way of viewing [[Connection (mathematics)|connections]] in terms of descent data from infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the diagonal.

==Introduction and motivation==
The Grothendieck connection is a generalization of the [[Gauss–Manin connection]] constructed in a manner analogous to that in which the [[Ehresmann connection]] generalizes the [[Covariant derivative#Koszul connection|Koszul connection]].  The construction itself must satisfy a requirement of ''geometric invariance'', which may be regarded as the analog of [[covariance]] for a wider class of structures including the [[Scheme (mathematics)|schemes]] of algebraic geometry.  Thus the connection in a certain sense must live in a natural [[Sheaf (mathematics)|sheaf]] on a [[Grothendieck topology]].  In this section, we discuss how to describe an Ehresmann connection in sheaf-theoretic terms as a Grothendieck connection.

Let <math>M</math> be a [[Manifold (mathematics)|manifold]] and <math>\pi : E \to M</math> a [[Surjective function|surjective]] [[Submersion (mathematics)|submersion]], so that <math>E</math> is a manifold fibred over <math>M.</math>  Let <math>J^1(M, E)</math> be the first-order [[jet bundle]] of sections of <math>E.</math>  This may be regarded as a bundle over <math>M</math> or a bundle over the total space of <math>E.</math>  With the latter interpretation, an Ehresmann connection is a section of the bundle (over <math>E</math>) <math>J^1(M, E) \to E.</math>  The problem is thus to obtain an intrinsic description of the sheaf of sections of this vector bundle.

Grothendieck's solution is to consider the diagonal embedding <math>\Delta : M \to M \times M.</math>  The sheaf <math>I</math> of ideals of <math>\Delta</math> in <math>M \times M</math> consists of functions on <math>M \times M</math> which vanish along the diagonal.  Much of the infinitesimal geometry of <math>M</math> can be realized in terms of <math>I.</math>  For instance, <math>\Delta^*\left(I, I^2\right)</math> is the sheaf of sections of the [[cotangent bundle]].  One may define a ''first-order infinitesimal neighborhood'' <math>M^{(2)}</math> of <math>\Delta</math> in <math>M \times M</math> to be the [[Scheme (mathematics)|subscheme]] corresponding to the sheaf of ideals <math>I^2.</math>  (See below for a coordinate description.)  

There are a pair of projections <math>p_1, p_2 : M \times M \to M</math> given by projection the respective factors of the Cartesian product, which restrict to give projections <math>p_1, p_2 : M^{(2)} \to M.</math>  One may now form the [[pullback bundle|pullback]] of the fibre space <math>E</math> along one or the other of <math>p_1</math> or <math>p_2.</math>  In general, there is no canonical way to identify <math>p_1^* E</math> and <math>p_2^* E</math> with each other.  A '''Grothendieck connection''' is a specified isomorphism between these two spaces. One may proceed to define [[Affine connection|curvature]] and [[p-curvature]] of a connection in the same language.
